scenarios.title: Wife anniversary — romantic + deep

request.primaryOccasionContext: Ten years of choosing each other on ordinary Tuesdays, not just the big days
request.details: You still save me the last piece of toast without making a speech about it

cards.text: Sara, this anniversary, for me, is about choosing each other on ordinary Tuesdays—not just the big days. It’s the quiet yes in the middle of real life, the way we meet each other where we are. And it shows up in the smallest places—like you still saving me the last piece of toast without making a speech about it. I notice. I carry it with me. Thank you for all those ordinary Tuesdays. I choose you next Tuesday, and the one after, and the one after that. I love you, Sara. Forever, Michael

scenarios.title: Husband apology — direct

request.primaryOccasionContext: I snapped at you about the weekend plans and you didn't deserve that
request.details: You were only trying to make Saturday easier for both of us

cards.text: David, I’m owning it: I snapped at you about the weekend plans, and you didn’t deserve that. You were only trying to make Saturday easier for both of us, and I made it harder. I let my stress do the talking. That wasn’t fair to you. Can we reset and look at Saturday together—no edge, just us figuring it out? I appreciate that you tried to help with Saturday. I see it, and I’m sorry for how I came at you. I'm sorry — Lena

scenarios.title: Auth-shaped Mom thank-you — rich + primary subject stress (body relAnswers only)

request.primaryOccasionContext: Helping me navigate the paperwork for new health insurance this month
request.details: You sat on hold for almost two hours so I wouldn't have to

relAnswers.parentPersonality: Tough, supportive, stubborn in the best way
relAnswers.parentFact: Always drops anything if one of us needs her

cards.text: Mom, thank you for helping me navigate the paperwork for my new health insurance this month. You even sat on hold for almost two hours so I wouldn’t have to — that tough, stubborn-in-the-best-way side of you put to work for me. I know that cost real time and patience. You took a confusing, draining process and made it manageable, and I felt the stress drop the moment you stepped in. I’m grateful not just that the coverage is getting squared away, but for the example you set of pushing through the hard, necessary things. I see it, I appreciate it, and I won’t forget it. Love, James

scenarios.title: Auth-shaped Husband anniversary — romantic rich (body relAnswers only)

request.primaryOccasionContext: Eight years in — still my favorite person to run errands with
request.details: Our terrible first apartment with the leaning stove still makes me laugh

relAnswers.spouseSmile: When you steal fries and deny it with a straight face

cards.text:
Marcus, you're still my favorite person to run errands with.
On our anniversary, that's the truest thing I know: grocery lists, returns, the slow aisle loops—ordinary minutes that feel right because it's you next to me.
I still laugh about that terrible first apartment with the leaning stove; somehow that kind of crooked start made me love our everyday even more.
And when you steal fries and deny it with a straight face, it gets me every time—because even the smallest moments with you are the ones I want.
If the rest of our days are carts, receipts, and picking the "fast" line together, I'm in. With you, the in‑between is the point. Still choosing you — Ava

request.primaryOccasionContext: You earned this diploma after nights of doubt and still showing up
request.details: Watching you present your senior project without shaking was a full-circle moment

relAnswers.proudOf: How she builds community around quieter classmates

cards.text:
Maya,
You earned this diploma the real way — through nights of doubt and still showing up.
Watching you present your senior project without shaking was a full-circle moment.
I see how you build community around quieter classmates — and I see that same choice to show up in how you earned this diploma. This diploma carries all of that.
As you step into what’s next, trust what you’ve already proven to yourself: you can meet the day, even when it’s hard. I’m so proud of the person I’m seeing right now. So proud — Dad

request.primaryOccasionContext: I canceled on your birthday dinner last-minute and that was selfish
request.details: You had already reserved the noisy corner table we like
request.signOff: Sorry — and thank you for still picking up — Sam

cards.text:
Dee, I’m sorry I canceled on your birthday dinner last-minute — that was selfish.
You’d already locked down the noisy corner table we like, and I still bailed. I get that it put you in a crappy spot on your own birthday.
I’m owning it, and I won’t do that again. If you’re up for it, dinner’s on me at that same loud corner — your call on timing. Sorry — and thank you for still picking up — Sam
